messages:
Leah: quick heads-up — I reproduced a p99 tail regression on stage during the midday multitenant run. baseline p95 ~220ms, p99 jumped from ~380ms to ~1.9s when concurrency hit ~600. suspecting KV cache eviction thrash + mb sizing interaction.
Ishaan: ugh. any flame graphs?
Leah: yeah grabbed a few. main signal is lots of threads blocked on kv::get_mutex and then spurts of kernel fallback. tried to attach a tiny snippet:
```
# simplified repro command
./loadgen --model redwood-v1 --qps 800 --concurrency 600 --input-dist hot10% cold90% --microbatch 8
```
Leah: profile dump shows ~48% time in kv lookup critical section during spikes, and a secondary cluster of time spent in "kernel_select() -> fallback_path".
Ben: microbatch=8 under high concurrent cold keys means more KV misses per microbatch and longer critical section while building KV lists? that could amplify lock hold time.
Marie: played with microbatch=1/2/4 on a node earlier — lowering to 4 pushed p99 down to ~650ms but throughput dropped ~12%. p95 barely moved.
Ishaan: so tradeoff: smaller mb reduces per-request tail but hurts aggregate throughput. does kernel selection change when cache miss rate increases?
Leah: yes — when KV miss rate > ~30% we saw a higher fraction of requests routed to the slower attention kernel (it avoids some fused paths that assume cached KV layout). also observed more memcpy stalls while filling KV buffers.
perf-ci: perf-ci bot: nightly multitenant-run finished, regressions detected: p99 increased by +480ms vs yesterday for stage cluster id=stg-eu-2.
Ben: we should instrument lock wait times (contention) per tenant and add a metric for "kv-evict-rate" per host. current metrics only show cache_size and hit_rate.
Marie: agreed. quick patch I tried: introduce a small eviction hysteresis and cap microbatch at 4 for tenants with cold-hot ratio > 5. config diff:
```
runtime:
  microbatch_max: 4
  kv_eviction_hysteresis: 0.12
  hotset_reserve_pct: 8
```
Leah: early A/B looked ok — p99 down 60% on the noisy tenant, overall throughput down 9%. still want a less blunt instrument.
Ishaan: idea: make kernel selection aware of recent cache_fault_rate on the worker. if worker sees a spike in cache evictions, prefer the kernel path that minimizes synchronous KV locks (async-KV path), even if slightly slower per-op, to reduce tail.
Ben: +1. and add microbatch gating: reject large microbatches on workers with >X ms lock wait per sec. basically dynamic cap.
Marie: will prototype: two changes — 1) per-worker dynamic_mb_cap based on last 30s avg lock-wait, 2) kernel_pref_score that includes cache_fault_rate.
Leah: can we also add a cheap predictive hotset prefetch for the top-N tokens per tenant so hot cold mix is less bursty? prefetching a tiny window reduced misses in my local runs.
Ishaan: beware of prefetch amplification under multitenant — we'll need tenant-level budget.
perf-ci: perf-ci bot: scheduled canary with dynamic_mb_cap and hysteresis tomorrow 09:00 UTC.
Ben: next steps:
- Marie to push prototype branch with metrics + dynamic_mb gating (PR by EOD)
- Ishaan to add kernel selection hook to consider cache_fault_rate (design doc inline)
- Leah will run larger stage run tomorrow + collect contention traces
- infra to expose kv_eviction_rate metric (infra-bot: ping)
Leah: also note: we should add a p99-tail incident playbook snippet: when p99 > 1s and kv_eviction_rate > threshold -> throttle microbatch globally for affected workers and route traffic to dedicated pool if available.
infra-bot: infra-bot: @eng-runtime flagged for kv_eviction_rate metric request (ticket#INF-3921).
Ishaan: thanks — going to sketch the kernel hook now. I'll post a short design in #eng-runtime later. :thumbsup:
Leah: awesome. filing a short postmortem-style thread after the canary.
Marie: sending PR in ~3h. :rocket:
